author: FChecklist
body:
AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'Tier-1 audit the never-audited duplication-blocked task identity retirement change' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  ...733-stop-the-duplicate-resubmission-loop-tha.md |  50 +++++++++
 ...846-tier-1-audit-the-never-audited-duplicati.md |  74 +++++++++++++
 scripts/resource_governor.py                       |  81 +++++++++++++--
 scripts/superboss-register.py                      | 115 ++++++++++++++++++++-
 tests/test_resource_governor.py                    | 108 +++++++++++++++++++
 5 files changed, 419 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: The rejected_duplicate-attempt-cap/retirement logic in resource_governor.submit() is directionally sound and its primary reproduced scenario (sustained active-row duplicate rejection up to the cap) is correctly tested, but the accompanying schema migration in superboss-register.py's new _migrate_umr_status_check() introduces a real, previously-untested concurrency hazard: it performs a destructive multi-statement table rebuild (DROP TRIGGER/DROP TABLE umr_tasks_fts, CREATE umr_tasks__migrate, INSERT...SELECT *, DROP TABLE umr_tasks, ALTER TABLE...RENAME) with no explicit transaction wrapper, and it is reachable via _ensure_umr_table() from at least four real call sites in resource_governor.py that use three different (or zero) concurrency-control mechanisms -- submit() holds superboss-register.py's cross-process sbr._write_lock() (DB_PATH+'.writelock'), dispatch_one() instead holds dispatch_core.py's entirely separate worker-spawn.lock, and --query-umr/scan_stuck_tasks()/_shed_load() take no lock at all around their _ensure_umr_table() call. Because this is a one-time migration that every concurrently-running governor process (cron sweeps, systemd timers, the watchdog, dispatch ticks) will hit at first deploy, this is a real, non-hypothetical race window for the exact multi-process unsynchronized-write corruption class this codebase already suffered a production SQLite corruption incident from on 2026-07-23 (documented directly in sbr._write_lock()'s own docstring, which is precisely why that lock exists). Neither the PR's own tests nor the prior worker's 'AUDIT:PASS' real-execution verification (explicitly single-process/sequential) exercised concurrent invocation of this migration, so this risk was never caught before merge. Secondarily, the retirement-cap check only re-fires on the 'duplicate blocked by an active row' code path, not on the 'no active row, fresh accept' path, so an identity whose cumulative rejected_duplicate count already reached/crossed the cap can still receive one more fresh 'queued' row if its blocking row happens to go terminal on the exact tick the cap would otherwise have been crossed -- this delays, rather than guarantees, permanent retirement in the edge case, contrary to the PR's 'never resubmitted again' claim. Given the first issue is a genuine data-corruption/crash risk in a file explicitly flagged as needing unusual care, and it already merged to main without being caught, this should not stand as approved as-is. Issues found: superboss-register.py's new _migrate_umr_status_check() runs a destructive DROP TABLE + rebuild + RENAME sequence on umr_tasks with no explicit transaction wrapper, and is reachable unsynchronized from resource_governor.py's --query-umr, scan_stuck_tasks(), and _shed_load() (no lock at all) as well as dispatch_one() (a *different* lock, dispatch_core's worker-spawn.lock, not superboss-register's own sbr._write_lock() that submit() uses) -- two or more real concurrent processes can race into this migration on first deploy, risking a crash (CREATE TABLE umr_tasks__migrate is not IF NOT EXISTS) or, on a crash/kill between DROP TABLE umr_tasks and the RENAME, permanently losing the umr_tasks table with no rollback -- the exact class of concurrent-unsynchronized-write corruption this repo already suffered in production on 2026-07-23 per _write_lock()'s own docstring. Not exercised by any test or by the prior audit's real-execution checks, which were explicitly single-process/sequential.; resource_governor.submit()'s retirement-cap check (attempt_count >= MAX_DUPLICATE_ATTEMPTS_PER_IDENTITY) only executes inside the 'existing active row found' branch; if an identity's blocking row happens to reach a terminal state on the exact tick that would have crossed the cap, submit() takes the plain 'no active row -> accept as new' path instead, creating a fresh queued row with no cap check at all -- so a poisoned identity is not deterministically guaranteed to be retired the moment its true attempt count crosses the cap, only eventually, contrary to the PR's stated 'never resubmitted again' guarantee. Untested by the PR's own new test, which only covers the case where the row stays active through every rejection up to the cap.; Minor: the per-submission attempt count is computed via query_umr_tasks(..., limit=1_000_000), fetching and materializing up to a million rows into memory rather than a SQL COUNT(*) -- an avoidable inefficiency inside the module whose entire purpose is guarding server resource exhaustion.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
